strokes.text: Most failures are the provider declining to act.
Each section quotes the message the provider prints and then names the cause.
Wrong Scene Collection
refusing OBS write/read: current collection
OBS has a different scene collection selected than the `collection` of the resource.
Select the right collection in OBS and plan again.
Unsupported Canvas
refusing mutation on unsupported live canvas
Set the base canvas to 1920x1080 under Settings, Video.
An Output Is Active
reports active output
Stop streaming, recording, the virtual camera and the replay buffer, then apply again.
No Connection Settings
no obs-websocket config found
The provider looked for the configuration file OBS writes and did not find one.
Enable the WebSocket server in OBS, or set `host`, `port` and `password` in @index.
Password Problems
obs-websocket requires a password and none was provided
Set `password` to the value shown in the WebSocket Server Settings of OBS.
A remote `host` always needs `password`, because the local configuration file describes only the local OBS.
Bridge Version Mismatch
ordinary obs-websocket version identity mismatch
Group resources run only against OBS 32.2.2 with obs-websocket 5.7.4; see @guides/groups.
A Filter Would Be Displaced
refusing to displace filter
The declared `index` is held by a filter the provider does not manage.
Choose a free position, or bring the other filter under management first.
A Plan That Never Comes Back Empty
Something else keeps changing a value that Terraform manages, such as a controller, a hotkey or an animation filter.
Decide which of the two owns the value, and remove it from the other.
A scene without @resources/scene_contents can also need a second plan before its layer order settles.
After a Timeout
Run a fresh plan when a write times out or reports an uncertain result.
The provider observes OBS again and plans from what it finds, and it does not replay the earlier write.
